steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2 1/2 x 8 1/2-inch loaf pan with butter. Whisk the flour, oats, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl; set aside.

Whisk the eggs in a mixing bowl until smooth. Beat in the bananas, sour cream, and melted butter. Add the sugar, cranberries, and lemon juice; beat until evenly blended. Fold into the oat mixture until no dry lumps remain. Pour into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Banana Oat Bread

review.reviewBody: i used whole wheat white flour, added just a touch of vanilla extract and used almost all organic ingredients. I took a previous reviewers advice and added in about a half cup (maybe more) of chopped pecans. I thought this was perfect. All the ingredient measurements were spot on, which I really appreciate. I actually made muffins out of this recipe (we're more of a muffin family than a loaf family) and I got twelve muffins that were a little on the bigger side. Right before baking, I pushed in a couple extra cranberries into the top of each muffin and sprinkled just a little extra chopped pecans on top. These baked up wonderfully and both kids and husband really enjoyed these.

I found this recipe years ago and still use it, it is great every time! I now make the batter and make muffins out of them. It makes more than a dozen, around 15. Check them after 20 min and then a few minutes after if it needs more time. Thanks for this!

This is good. I had to use vanilla yogurt in place of sour cream, and I tend to like things less sweet, so I ended up decreasing the sugar to about 1/3 cup. It is still pretty sweet, largely because of the dried cranberries. I did add walnuts, and I cooked it in three mini bread pans. Next time I will probably add cinnamon and vanilla for a bit more flavor. I might try a mix of dried cranberries and fresh ones to cut the sweetness and add some tang.
I added 1 tablespoon of chai seeds and I had some puréed kale and add about half a cup to it. It turned out real good. I will make this again.

That is some yummy banana bread! 
I "healthyfied" the recipe and used whole-wheat flour, applesauce instead of butter and added 1/2 cup chopped walnuts. The bread is moist and the tartness of the cranberries compliments well the sweetness of the bananas. 
Will sure make that again!
used this recipe for muffins, they were amazing! i used vanilla yogurt instead of sour cream and added 1/4 cup extra mashed bananas . also added 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts.

This bread came out so moist! It was great! I changed just a few things. I added 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1 tsp of vanilla. I also didn't have dried cranberries on hand so I just didn't add them. It came out sooooo good. In the future I want to try a few things to get the top of the crust to brown up a little more - just for presentation. Maybe some egg-yolk or butter brushed on? I'll have to see. Definitely making this again!

This was an easy recipe to put together. I did add about 1/4 cup of brown sugar due to some reviews stating it was not quite sweet enough. I added golden raisins because I was out of cranberries. The taste of the bread is really nice. Next time I am going to be sure to have cranberries on hand! Thanks for sharing this recipe
Excellent recipe! I did substitute nonfat yogurt for the sour cream and melted butter, and it turned out wonderful. Will definitely use this recipe again.

Since I didn't have the exact ingredients, I did a little custominzing: 1 cup fresh cranberries, 1 cup banana, 1/4 cup applesauce, 2 tbsp whipped cream cheese, 1/3 cup canola oil. Still turned out wonderful!

Made this today and it is OMG good!!!!!! Used fresh cranberries as that's what I had on hand.Heavy sprinkle of chopped walnuts on top before baking. Love the combo, will make again &again.thanks for the great recipe:):):)

I agree with other reviewers who say it's a bit bland. It's also heavy. I added vanilla, as well as pecans, but it needs a little more something. Using brown sugar would make it a bit better, I think.

I wanted a banana walnut cranberry bread. I followed the directions pretty much. But I didn't have sour cream nor yogurt nor apple sauce. So I added Fruit cocktail. And I used frozen/thawed whole cranberries. That was the only change. With my stove I had to increase cook time by 10 minutes. Just kind of watched it. It was really good. Thank you for this recipe! I will save it to my favorites and use again! TerriB
Worked out pretty well. I ended up using sour cream instead of the yogurt and added a cup of cranberries and raisins mixed together.
To die for. I put extra bananas , a bit more anyway. It’s really good.

This has become our family's go-to banana bread recipe. The dried cranberries really do pair well with the sweetness of the bananas. I've experimented with the recipe over time, and the only changes I consistently make are to substitute whole wheat for all-purpose flour and coconut oil for butter. Enjoy!
The only change I made was to add walnuts, otherwise, the recipe was perfect.

This is a tasty breakfast bread. I was skeptical of the large amount of baking powder, but it worked. Followed the instructions pretty closely, only switched lemon juice for grated orange peel. The oats make it more substantial, than regular flour. I would make it again.
I used dried cherries instead of cranberries (my husband cannot eat them) and added chopped pecans. This will be my "go to" banana bread recipe from now on! It is delicious!
A very tasty change from your standard banana bread...no need to make any changes to the recipe as written. Will make this again for Christmas morning,
